subject: Recovery verification and artifact request - TrustBank vendor assessment
messages:
From: Lenora Briggs <lenora.briggs@trustbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@trustbank.com
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: recovery verification artifacts & RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Rishi,

TrustBank is progressing through its third-party security assessment for our upcoming production connection. Our risk team has requested the following artifacts to validate your BCP/DR posture and RTO/RPO claims: 

- Recent RTO/RPO test results (last 12 months) with timestamps and pass/fail criteria.
- Post-mortem or tabletop notes for any incident in the last 18 months that involved cross-region failover.
- A concise recovery runbook (customer-facing) showing steps to restore service and expected timelines.
- KV cache warm-up timings and any measured cold-start vs warm-start token latency deltas.
- Confirmation of restore capacity (GPUs/nodes) and the process for activating reserved capacity.

Can you provide these artifacts by end of day Monday, Sep 27? If any items require an NDA or separate download link, please call that out. We may ask follow-up questions after review.

Thanks,
Lenora Briggs
Senior Vendor Risk Analyst
TrustBank

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lenora Briggs <lenora.briggs@trustbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: recovery verification artifacts & RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Lenora —

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching a consolidated package and linking what we can in Drive. Quick mapping below so you can jump to the files you asked for: 

- RTO/RPO test results: attached as rto-rpo-test-results.csv (tabular dump of automated run output; includes timestamps, sequence lengths, and measured restore times).
- Post-mortems/tabletops: included in recovery-evidence-2026-09-25.zip under /tabletops/ (tabletop-summary.pdf + incident-postmortems).
- Customer-facing runbook: Drive link (pdf) + runbook excerpt included in the zip under /runbooks/customer_runbook_v2.pdf.
- KV warm-cache timings: kv-warm-cache-timings.pdf (attached) — summary page + raw logs.
- Restore capacity process: short playbook in the zip under /capacity/restore_capacity.md; TL;DR: Reserved fleet can be scaled to target capacity within 18 minutes with automated orchestration; manual escalation path is described in the doc.

Delivery ETA: We bundled everything we can share publicly in the zip. A couple of internal telemetry exports (redacted) are available via the shared Drive link; if TrustBank requires an executed NDA for those, let us know and we'll route via DocuSign.

Call to action: if helpful we can do a 30-minute walkthrough next week to run through the test artifacts and warm-cache numbers. Proposed times: Mon 9/28 10:00-10:30 PT or Tue 9/29 14:00-14:30 PT. 

Attachments: recovery-evidence-2026-09-25.zip, rto-rpo-test-results.csv, kv-warm-cache-timings.pdf

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: recovery verification artifacts & RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Lenora — thanks for the list. Two quick clarifications so we make sure the artifacts answer the risk team's questions: 

1) KV warm-cache timings: the attached PDF contains both aggregate percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and the raw per-run CSV excerpt. The key metric you asked about is the observed token latency delta when the KV cache is empty vs warmed; we include a dedicated summary table on page 2.

2) RTO test scope: the CSV includes both automated cold-start restores (full environment spin-up) and warm-recovery tests (service processes + cache warm) — see the \"test_type\" column. If you want us to separate out only customer-impacting scenarios, we can produce a distilled one-page summary.

3) Capacity: the restore_capacity.md has both automatic and manual escalation paths; our operational commitment for Dedicated customers is documented (time-to-reserve + activation).

If helpful, I'm happy to take the walkthrough and bring a runtime engineer to answer deeper questions on cache priming. I can make Tue 9/29 14:00 PT work. Would that suit your team?

--
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
